Hi there, I'm using celery with SQS and having the same issue with the `countdown` 30 min in `apply_async` args. Please, if you could prioritise this bug, then this would be a great help!

After a lot of testing I found that in order changes in  `visibility_timeout` value to take effect, one must set it in all, celery config, result backend & transport options, as follows :
`   
visibility_timeout = 600
`
`
result_backend_transport_options = broker_transport_options = {
    'visibility_timeout': 600
}
`
So the reported behavior might not be a product defect per se, just lack of proper documentation

> After a lot of testing I found that in order changes in `visibility_timeout` value to take effect, one must set it in all, celery config, result backend & transport options, as follows : ` visibility_timeout = 600` `result_backend_transport_options = broker_transport_options = { 'visibility_timeout': 600 }` So the reported behavior might not be a product defect per se, just lack of proper documentation

would you mind sending a PR to improve the documentation?

To those using rabbitmq as broker, please checkout the "Warning" section under "Calling - ETA and Countdown".
https://docs.celeryq.dev/en/stable/userguide/calling.html#eta-and-countdown
Due to rabbitmq version updates, your rabbitmq config may need to be updated to bump the consumer timeout to a very large value, e.g. `consumer_timeout = 31622400000`.

in ubuntu, you can set this variable in `/etc/rabbitmq/rabitmq-env.conf` by adding the below line.
`RABBITMQ_SERVER_ADDITIONAL_ERL_ARGS="-rabbit consumer_timeout 31622400000"`
https://stackoverflow.com/a/73928874/868736

issue.title: Improve documentation on visibility timeout
issue.body:
## Description

Updated documentation to make it more obvious and clear how to set visibility timeout for Redis broker.

Need to set ALL the values (not clear in documentation still) for it to take effect, and conflicts between apps cause issues

Per https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/7651 and https://github.com/celery/celery/issues/5935

body:
```python
import datetime as dt
import time
import numpy as np
import tqdm
from celery import Celery
from kombu import Queue, Exchange

app = Celery(
    f"Celery app",
    broker= "redis://localhost:6379/0",
    backend="redis://localhost:6379/1",
)
app.conf.update(
    task_acks_late=True,  # ack only when task is finished
    visibility_timeout=14400,  # 4 hours
    worker_pool_restarts=True,  # restarting by remote control
    worker_max_tasks_per_child=1,
    worker_max_memory_per_child=1024 * 1024,  # 1GB
    worker_prefetch_multiplier=1,  # prefetch 1 task per worker
    worker_concurrency=10,  # will be overridden by autoscale
    broker_heartbeat=60,
    broker_connection_retry=True,
    broker_connection_retry_on_startup=True,
    broker_connection_max_retries=0,
    broker_connection_timeout=10,
    broker_transport_options={"visibility_timeout": 14400},  # 4 hours
    result_backend_transport_options={"visibility_timeout": 14400},  # 4 hours
    task_queues=(
        Queue("queue_a"),
        Queue("queue_b"),
    ),
    task_routes={
        f"run_a": {"queue": "queue_a"},
        f"run_b": {"queue": "queue_b"},
    },
)

@app.task(name="test_visibility_timeout", queue="queue_a")
def test_visibility_timeout(num: int):
    print("test_visibility_timeout started at", dt.datetime.now())
    # Custom tqdm update: only update progress every 10 seconds to reduce log spam
    with tqdm.tqdm(total=num) as pbar:
        last_update = time.time()
        last_i = 0
        for i in range(num):
            if time.time() - last_update >= 10 or i == num - 1:
                pbar.update(i + 1 - last_i)
                last_i = i + 1
                last_update = time.time()
        x = np.random.rand() + np.random.rand()
    print("test_visibility_timeout finished at", dt.datetime.now())
    return "Hello, World!"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    test_visibility_timeout.delay(int(1.2e10))
```
